articles.summary: Women make up a majority of the college-educated labor force in the U.S., according to Pew Research Survey . This factor could partly explain why they are also a rising share of managers and professionals , although there is still room to grow in their representation in top executive roles—a working paper from a World Bank economist found that only 16% of CFOs and 7% of CEOs in large U.S. and European companies were women in 2023. articles.title: The Best Companies for Future Leaders 2027
articles.summary: The career paths of future leaders may look markedly different than they did a decade ago, as AI becomes increasingly commonplace and new startups disrupt legacy corporations as early career hotspots. TIME and Statista partnered on the fourth edition of the Best Companies for Future Leaders to highlight the career stepping stones that shaped over 5,900 influential U.S.-based leaders from business, government, academia and society, with emerging younger leaders added to the research list each year. articles.title: How TIME and Statista Determined the Best Companies and Colleges for Future Leaders 2027
articles.summary: In the fourth edition of The Best Colleges and Companies for Future Leaders, TIME and Statista have ranked the 175 companies and 125 colleges that stand out in the career and education histories of U.S. leaders. The list draw on approximately 5,900 influential U.S.-based leaders from business, government, academia, and society. They do not measure reputation or survey opinion. articles.title: When People Keep What Surgeons Remove
articles.summary: Emily likes her uterus much better in a jar than in her body. The 20-year-old, who asked to be identified by her first name to protect her privacy, keeps it in her bedroom, on what she calls her “dead things table,” among animal skulls and other specimens. After years of difficult symptoms, she had a hysterectomy at 19—and made arrangements to bring the organ home.
